facts.statement: Article 1 (definitions) adds 'special underwriting' (特定引受け) to the terms defined by reference to Article 16-2(1) of the Trade Insurance Act; no other defined term changes. New Article 5-2 requires Nippon Export and Investment Insurance (NEXI), when seeking the METI Minister's approval of a special underwriting decision under Article 16-4(2) of the Act, to submit an application stating (i) the content of the trade insurance or reinsurance concerned and (ii) the matters needed to confirm whether the underwriting relates to an arrangement designated by the METI Minister under Article 16-2(1). Before the amendment the regulation contained no provision on special underwriting, because the statutory category itself was created by Act No. 29 of 2026.

The amendment directly binds only Nippon Export and Investment Insurance (the 'Company' under the Trade Insurance Act): it prescribes what NEXI must file when it seeks ministerial approval of a special underwriting decision. It imposes no direct filing or other duty on exporters, lenders or project sponsors; they are affected indirectly, because cover for a transaction linked to a designated government-to-government arrangement can only be underwritten through this approval route.

Obligation (mandatory). Article 5-2 uses 'must submit' (提出しなければならない): filing an application containing the two listed items is a precondition of the approval that Article 16-4(2) of the Act requires before NEXI decides on a special underwriting. It is not a recommendation or best-efforts duty.
The amending instrument's supplementary provisions contain no transitional provision.

Implements, and does not further delegate. Article 5-2 supplies the filing content for the approval procedure that Article 16-4(2) of the Trade Insurance Act requires; the regulation itself leaves no matter to a further instrument. (At Act level, Article 16-2(1) leaves designation of qualifying government-to-government arrangements to the METI Minister, exercised by Notice No. 96 of 2026, and Articles 16-2 and 16-3 require the Minister to set and publish the special underwriting business guidelines and standards, Notices Nos. 97 and 98 of 2026.)

METI's official explanation of the 2026 bill presents the special underwriting business as a response to supply-chain vulnerability exposed by geopolitical risk: cover for transactions under government-to-government arrangements judged particularly necessary for the resilience of Japanese companies' supply chains, designed with the Japan-United States strategic investment initiative in view. The statutory design separates the new business from ordinary underwriting (prior ministerial approval, published guidelines and standards, a segregated special account, and interest-free government bonds of up to 3 trillion yen deliverable until 31 March 2029) so that strategically motivated, potentially large exposures do not silently draw on the ordinary trade insurance account.

For exporters, lenders and sponsors, the practical effect is a new, approval-gated route to Japanese official cover for projects under a designated arrangement: eligibility turns on the arrangement and the published special underwriting standards, not on the ordinary underwriting criteria, and each decision needs the METI Minister's prior approval, which adds a government decision point (and its timing) to transaction planning. For NEXI, the business is ring-fenced in a special account supported by deliverable government bonds, which changes how the risk is capitalised compared with ordinary lines.
